note: These prompts are invented test cases. They are written in the style of the user, but the situations are not real. In particular, the mortgage figures in eval 0 are example values and are not anyone's real loan.

evals.name: refinance-break-even
evals.prompt: explain to me how mortgage refinance break even works. i have a 30 year loan, $520,000 balance at 6.8%, 28 years left, and thinking about refinance to 6.1% with closing cost about $6,000. make it html so i can read it
evals.expected_output: One self-contained HTML page that explains the break-even calculation with the user's own numbers, step by step, with correct arithmetic.
expectations: Every sentence has 25 words or fewer
No idioms or informal expressions (from a list of about 150)
No Latin abbreviations (e.g., i.e., etc., vs.) and no ambiguous dates
No contractions (don't, it's, you'll)
At most 2 phrasal verbs or uncommon words from the checker lists
The page is one self-contained file (no external font, script, style, or image)
No decorative emoji or symbol characters
The page starts with a short answer that states the conclusion and the key numbers, before any background
A concrete worked example with real numbers comes before the general rule or formula
Each step of the worked example states its reason
Each key term is defined in visible text in the sentence where it first appears
Each key concept keeps one name on the whole page (no synonym variation)
All essential content is visible without a click or hover (only self-check answers or optional depth may be hidden)
The page has self-check questions with hidden answers, and each answer includes the reasoning
The page names a common wrong idea and explains why it fails
The page states the limits or assumptions of the explanation
Each important number has a source or a stated calculation method, with a confidence level
The page has at least one explanatory figure, the title of the figure states the finding as a sentence, and the labels are inside the figure
Two cases are compared side by side, and the principle is stated after the comparison
The current monthly payment is stated as $3,465.75 (tolerance $1), and the break-even result equals the closing cost divided by the monthly saving that the page states
The page states which term the new loan has (30 years or 28 years) and shows how that choice changes the result
